title: Work reads: read the operator-configured, validated Engram store without a live agent session binding
outcome:
Greg (2026-09-15, via Codex #1798): 'this is a huge gap, the feature is unusable. Beads are working fine.' Reproduced read-only on the running host: GET /api/projects/project-13/work (PhoenixCodeNav, local, Engram enabled, .engram-project present, home C:/Users/grzeg/.engram, engram.db 168513536 bytes) returns engram=unavailable 'No established matching host session binding/store; this view does not create one', readerSessionId=null, page=null.

ROOT CAUSE (source): AppState::work_read_snapshot (src/work_visualizer.rs:24-68) builds the read target only from a live local SessionRecord whose runtime-only engram_mcp_installed descriptor matches engram_mcp_runtime_config_for_session_locked. That descriptor is cleared by clear_runtime and initialised to None from persisted state, so after a host restart, or whenever no agent session is bound in the project, the view has no reader. docs/features/work-visualizer.md lines 91-92 wrote this down as the contract ('Bindings are runtime-only ... the view reports unavailable'); the first scope deliberately reused agent bindings and the accepted mock never showed the no-session case. That contract is wrong for the product: an operator-enabled project with a doctor-validated store must be viewable at any time.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS WITHOUT A SESSION: EngramProjectSettings (persisted per project) carries enabled, binary_path, home and authority_store_key (project_id + canonical database_path, set by the enablement doctor, cleared at load only when .engram-project is gone). validate_work_read_target (src/work_visualizer.rs ~270-322) already verifies everything from project-level data: declaration == store.project_id, HOME/projects/SHA256(project_id)/engram.db canonicalises to the admitted path (tm-m6r1.9 stays intact), store file exists and is non-empty. The only inputs the session descriptor adds are the CLI identity flags: work --actor-id A --session-id S (run_work_read_command, src/work_visualizer_process.rs:36-47).

ENGRAM READ IDENTITY SEMANTICS (verified 2026-09-15 against C:/github/Personal/Engram @6ac411b and engram 0.1.0 build adb6ea807c12 on PATH; the project's configured binary must be re-checked by the implementer): --actor-id / --session-id / --actor-context are optional for every work word and default from the OS user + one stable per-process id; --mine is the only identity-relative list filter and the Work view uses --all; --actor-context never changes assignment/claim/handoff identity; the --after cursor encodes project/session context, so continuations need the SAME session id. work_service/service.rs: read_store_at -> lock_store_at only validates attribution (non-empty actor and session, storage::admit_session_id, validate_process_default_work_session) and opens the store; ONLY store_at (stateful verbs) calls initialize_process_default_work_session, and only for session ids inside PROCESS_DEFAULT_WORK_SESSION_NAMESPACE. So an explicit, stable host session id outside that namespace, used only for ls/show, registers nothing and mutates nothing (the existing WAL/empty-store caveat in the doc still applies and is already guarded by the non-empty store precheck).

REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR (Greg): read the explicitly configured, validated existing Engram project store independently of running agent sessions, including immediately after restart. Keep no-init / no-enable / no-claim / no-tracker-mutation. Starting an agent is not the workaround.

DESIGN PROPOSAL:
1. Host reader target. In work_read_snapshot build the WorkReadTarget from project data: local project, remote_id == LOCAL, not in engram_project_resets, .engram-project present (metadata, as today), settings.is_base_enabled(), settings.binary_path, settings.home, settings.authority_store_key all present; connection.actor_id = a host seat in the existing grammar '{developer_name}/termal' (engram_seat_id uses '{developer}/{agent-kind}'), actor_context = None or 'agent=termal;role=work-view', session_id = one fixed id such as 'termal-work-view' (<= 64 bytes, outside the process-default namespace, stable across restarts so cursors stay valid). Then the unchanged validate_work_read_target runs before and after each read. Recommendation: make the host reader the ONLY Work reader (deterministic, restart-stable, no dependence on which agent happens to be running); keeping live-binding preference as a fallback is possible but adds a second identity for the same rows. Decision for Greg/owner.
2. Reader key on the wire. readerSessionId today is a session id and the detail/continuation routes look the session up again. For the host reader return a stable opaque key that cannot collide with a session id, e.g. 'host:' + short SHA-256 of (binary_path, home, store project_id, database_path, actor_id, session_id); continuation/detail with a key that no longer matches the current project configuration -> 409 'discard pages and refresh' (same semantics as a changed binding today). UI already treats the value as opaque (use-work-list.ts, WorkItemDetails.tsx); consider renaming the field to readerId in the same change or documenting the host: form.
3. Docs: replace the 'Bindings are runtime-only ... reports unavailable' paragraph and the HTTP table's readerSessionId wording; state the host reader identity, that reads never register a session (cite read_store_at), and that binary/home/store still come only from operator settings (never caller-supplied).
4. Tests (fixture-based, no clock dependence): enabled project + existing store + ZERO sessions -> engram ready, page served, readerSessionId = host key; same after clear_runtime (restart) -> still ready; disabled -> disabled; store file missing/empty -> unavailable and NOT created; declaration mismatch -> unavailable; continuation with a stale host key -> 409; host key never equals any session id; the fixture must assert the exact argv (--actor-id/--session-id values) so the identity is pinned.
5. Live acceptance on the actual host (Greg's requirement): after a host restart with no agent session in project-13, GET /api/projects/project-13/work returns engram ready with rows, the Work tab renders them, a detail read and a continuation work, and the store shows no new session row / no mutation attributable to the view. Requires deploy/restart, which is outside implementation authority.

OUT OF SCOPE: Beads (Greg: works; leave unchanged). Ownership: Codex holds the Work changes since #1795; this item records the diagnosis and design so either owner can implement once Greg assigns.
disposal_reason: Backlog triage w-930e4d333f07 (Architect1 batch 1a, spot-checked by Termal::Fable2): CLOSE-DONE. Live acceptance by Greg on 2026-09-15 (note 01a0a730); behaviour documented in engram-host-adapter.md :57-60. Closed by evidence.
